title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typescript page of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), page 83 of the exposé (§7.1.3). It is not part of the handwritten De Rham notes; the neighbouring manuscript pages, on derived categories modulo negligible objects, are unrelated. Note: the identification with the printed SGA 7 IX §7.1 rests on the 'IX' header, the page number and the references to VIII 3.5 and EGA III 5.4.5; I have not checked the printed text line by line.

Setting (semi-stable reduction, SGA 7 IX §7): S is the spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring and S_n are its truncations. G is the Néron model (or its identity component) of an abelian variety, and G_n = G ×_S S_n. After quotienting by the toric part one gets abelian schemes B_n over S_n, forming a formal abelian scheme B̂. The A_n are the related group schemes appearing in Exposé VIII.

Goal: show that B̂ is algebraizable. By Grothendieck's existence theorem (EGA III 5.4.5), it suffices to find a compatible system of invertible sheaves M_n on B_n with M_0 ample.

- The naive approach is to take an ample L on G and descend each restriction L_n to B_n. Grothendieck says he does not know whether such descents exist, and doubts it.
- Instead he builds a compatible system of polarizations ρ_n of the B_n. A polarization λ determines canonically the symmetric line bundle (1,λ)^*P, whose class is 2λ (the 'double'). Because these bundles are canonical, they automatically glue as n varies.
- An element of NS(B_n/S_n) is read as a symmetric divisorial correspondence, i.e. a symmetric biextension of (B_n,B_n) by G_m.
- By VIII 3.5, such biextensions correspond bijectively to biextensions of (A_n,A_n) by G_m.
- So one starts from a single symmetric biextension W of (A,A) by G_{m,S} (7.1.4) and base-changes it to each S_n.
- One must also assume that the class defined by W_0 is a polarization of B_0. One then obtains a polarization of B̂, hence an ample M̂ and algebraizability.
errors: The text says 'partir d'un Module inversible ample M de G' but then speaks of 'la restriction L_n de L'. M and L are used inconsistently (typo in the typescript).
'polarisation de B' should presumably read 'polarisation de B̂' (a formal object).
The subscript in 'par G_{m S}' for (A_n,A_n) presumably should be G_{m S_n}; it is harmless if read via base change.

ideas.what: Algebraize a formal abelian scheme via a compatible ample line bundle (Grothendieck existence theorem, EGA III 5.4.5)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck existence / formal GAGA for formal abelian schemes
ideas.where_published: EGA III 5.4.5; SGA 7 I Exp. IX §7

ideas.what: Use polarizations (whose doubles give canonical symmetric line bundles) instead of line bundles, so that compatibility in n is automatic
ideas.modern_name: Polarization vs. line bundle; (1,λ)^*P has class 2λ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (Abelian Varieties, GIT); Grothendieck in SGA 7

ideas.what: Néron–Severi elements as symmetric biextensions by G_m, transported between B_n and A_n via VIII 3.5
ideas.modern_name: Biextensions and polarizations; Raynaud/Mumford degeneration data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 VII–VIII); later Mumford 1972, Raynaud, Faltings–Chai
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. VII, VIII, IX §7

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX §7.1.3, misfiled among the De Rham notes. Its content (polarizations via biextensions to algebraize the abelian part in semi-stable reduction) is in print and well known.
transcription_corrections: Header '- 83 -  IX' is the SGA 7 Exposé IX page number, not a note page.
In the typescript, L_n and L appear underlined while the preceding sentence says M (the transcription is faithful; the inconsistency is the author's).
'(B_n,B_n) par G_{m S_n}' is correct; the later 'par G_{mS}' is as typed.
